title: Remediate shadowed prefix entries after rehash during rolling deploys
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a rolling canary deploy of runtime-1.19 we observed a slow, sustained memory increase on a subset of serving replicas which culminated in several OOM kills under normal traffic patterns. A portion of inference requests also returned stale values from the prefix KV layer (incorrect token prefixes), causing degraded output quality for ~12 minutes before automatic fallback kicked in. Impact: increased host memory, OOM restarts, degraded generation quality and increased latency; affected 8% of requests across the canary shard window; customer-facing errors were mitigated via automatic fallback but internal SLOs were breached. Root cause hypothesis: an uncoordinated prefix rehash path in the new index migration logic allowed a race where a new prefix index swap left behind "shadow" entries on old slabs that the eviction and TTL sweep logic no longer recognized. The rehash path used a lockless compare-and-swap to update the active index pointer, but replicas applying the migration concurrently could observe intermediate states where the active index referenced a different slab layout than the per-replica allocation maps. This produced unreachable entries: key metadata remained on-slab but the in-memory index no longer had a pointer; eviction logic skipped these entries because reference accounting relied on the index. TTL-refresh workers also skipped shadowed entries because their scan assumed index reachability. Combined, this created a population of unreachable entries that grew until memory pressure triggered OOM. Additional contributing factor: insufficient telemetry to surface unreachable-entry growth and no automated sweep job for index-shadowed entries. Evidence: heap profiles, slab allocation traces, and the canary host logs show monotonically increasing "slab_unmapped_entries" in the minutes after deploy; we reproduced a small repro locally by toggling index swap ordering and simulated concurrent alloc/free. Immediate remediation taken: rolled back the canary campaign to pre-1.19, pushed an emergency patch to make the index-swap atomic across the replica manager, and enabled a temporary aggressive sweep loop to reclaim shadowed entries. Current status: temporary sweep is in place; emergency patch is in canary and under observation. Next: implement robust fix and tests, add telemetry and a permanent periodic sweep job, update deploy rollout checks to prevent the race, and add post-deploy validation checks to detect reachable/unreachable entry divergence.
